title: Job Chapter 27 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Job chapter 27 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Job Chapter 27 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Job Chapter 27.

questions.question: In Job 27, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The first event in Job 27 is Job continuing his parable as stated in Job 27:1.

questions.question: What does Job claim God has taken away?
questions.explanation: Job states in Job 27:2 that 'who hath taken away my judgment'.

questions.question: What does Job say is in his nostrils?
questions.explanation: According to Job 27:3, 'the spirit of God is in my nostrils'.

questions.question: What will Job's lips not speak?
questions.explanation: Job declares in Job 27:4, 'My lips shall not speak wickedness'.

questions.question: What does Job refuse to do until he dies?
questions.explanation: Job states in Job 27:5 that 'till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me'.

questions.question: What does Job hold fast to?
questions.explanation: In Job 27:6, Job says, 'My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go'.

questions.question: Let mine enemy be as what, according to Job?
questions.explanation: Job expresses in Job 27:7, 'Let mine enemy be as the wicked'.

questions.question: What is the hope of the hypocrite?
questions.explanation: Job questions in Job 27:8, 'For what is the hope of the hypocrite, though he hath gained?' implying it is nonexistent.

questions.question: Who has vexed Job's soul?
questions.explanation: Job states in Job 27:2 that 'the Almighty, who hath vexed my soul'.

questions.question: As long as Job lives, what will his heart not do?
questions.explanation: Job claims in Job 27:6, 'my heart shall not reproach me so long as I live'.

questions.question: What does Job declare he will not speak?
questions.explanation: In Job 27:4, Job states, 'My lips shall not speak wickedness'.

questions.question: Job's soul is affected by whom?
questions.explanation: Job states in Job 27:2 that 'the Almighty, who hath vexed my soul', indicating his soul is affected.

questions.question: Job will justify his friends until he dies.
questions.explanation: Job clearly states in Job 27:5, 'God forbid that I should justify you: till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me'.

questions.question: Job holds fast to his wealth.
questions.explanation: Job holds fast to his righteousness, not his wealth, as indicated in Job 27:6.

questions.question: Job's heart reproaches him as long as he lives.
questions.explanation: Job states in Job 27:6 that 'my heart shall not reproach me so long as I live', indicating it does not reproach him.

medium.title: Job Chapter 27 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Job Chapter 27 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Will God hear the cry of a wicked man when trouble comes upon him?
questions.explanation: Job 27:9 indicates that God will not hear the cry of the wicked when trouble comes upon them.

questions.question: What does Job 27:10 promise will happen if someone delights himself in the Almighty?
options: He will always call upon God
He will live a long life
questions.correctAnswer: He will always call upon God
questions.explanation: Job 27:10 states that if a person delights in God, they will call upon Him consistently.

questions.question: What does Job claim he will teach based on the hand of God?
questions.explanation: In Job 27:11, Job declares he will teach truth as revealed by God's hand.

questions.question: What does Job ask concerning the behavior of his companions in Job 27:12?
questions.explanation: Job 27:12 poses the question of why his companions are altogether vain despite having seen the truth.

questions.question: What is described as the portion of a wicked man with God?
questions.explanation: Job 27:13 explicitly states that the heritage of oppressors is the portion of a wicked man with God.

questions.question: What shall happen to the children of a wicked man according to Job 27:14?
options: They will be multiplied for the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They will be multiplied for the sword
questions.explanation: Job 27:14 states that the children of a wicked man will be multiplied for destruction, symbolized by the sword.

questions.question: What does Job say about the remaining ones of a wicked man in Job 27:15?
options: They will be buried in death
questions.correctAnswer: They will be buried in death
questions.explanation: Job 27:15 indicates that those who remain will face death and their widows will not weep for them, showing their fate.

questions.question: What does Job say about wealth in Job 27:16?
questions.explanation: Job 27:16 highlights that even if a wicked man heaps up wealth, it does not provide true security or salvation.

questions.question: What does Job 27:6 say he holds fast to?
questions.explanation: Job 27:6 states that he holds fast to his integrity and will not let it go.

questions.question: What does Job equate with the hope of the hypocrite in Job 27:8?
questions.explanation: Job 27:8 questions the hope of the hypocrite in the context of having gained wealth without righteousness.

questions.question: What must Job not do according to Job 27:5?
questions.explanation: Job 27:5 emphasizes that he will not speak wickedness or justify his companions.

questions.question: What is Job's stance toward his enemies as stated in Job 27:7?
options: He wants them to be as the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: He wants them to be as the wicked
questions.explanation: Job 27:7 expresses Job's desire for his enemies to be treated as the wicked, indicating his feelings toward them.

questions.question: Is it true that Job believes his integrity will remain as long as he lives?
questions.explanation: Job 27:6 affirms that his heart will not reproach him as long as he maintains his integrity.

questions.question: Is it true that God delights in the wicked?
questions.explanation: The context of Job 27 implies that God does not delight in the wicked, as their fate is destruction.

questions.question: Is it true that Job claims he will conceal what is with the Almighty?
questions.explanation: Job 27:11 states that he will not conceal the truth that he teaches about God, indicating transparency.

hard.title: Job Chapter 27 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Job Chapter 27.

questions.question: According to Job 27:17, who shall put on what the rich man prepares?
questions.explanation: According to Job 27:17, 'He may prepare it, but the just shall put it on...' This indicates that the just will ultimately benefit from what the rich man prepares.

questions.question: Job 27:18 compares the rich man's house to what?
questions.explanation: Job 27:18 states, 'He buildeth his house as a moth,' implying the fragility and impermanence of the rich man's wealth.

questions.question: What happens to the rich man when he lies down, according to Job 27:19?
questions.explanation: Job 27:19 says, 'The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered,' indicating a loss of security and finality in death.

questions.question: In Job 27:20, what takes hold of the rich man?
questions.explanation: Job 27:20 states, 'Terrors take hold on him as waters,' suggesting overwhelming fear and anxiety in the face of his fate.

questions.question: What does Job 27:21 say carries the rich man away?
questions.explanation: Job 27:21 says, 'The east wind carrieth him away,' indicating the sudden and destructive nature of his downfall.

questions.question: What do men do to the rich man in Job 27:23?
questions.explanation: Job 27:23 states, 'Men shall clap their hands at him,' which signifies mockery and scorn for the fallen rich man.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'rasha' in Job 27:7 mean?
questions.explanation: 'Rasha' refers to someone who is morally wrong or wicked, as seen in Job 27:7, where Job contrasts himself with the wicked.

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Job 27:19-20 when describing the fate of the rich man?
questions.explanation: Job 27:19-20 uses metaphorical language to describe the rich man's fate, comparing his downfall to a lack of gathering and the overwhelming nature of terrors.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of the fate of the wicked in Job 27:13?
questions.explanation: Psalm 1:6 states, 'For the Lord knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish,' echoing the themes found in Job 27:13 regarding the fate of the wicked.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of justice found in Job 27:6?
questions.explanation: Romans 2:6 states, 'Who will repay each according to his works,' aligning with Job 27:6's assertion of maintaining integrity and righteousness.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Job 27:19?
questions.explanation: Job 27:19 follows directly after Job 27:18, where it discusses how the rich man's house is fragile, leading to the consequences mentioned.

questions.question: According to Job 27:10, does the wicked man delight in God?
questions.explanation: Job 27:10 asks, 'Will he delight himself in the Almighty?' implying that the wicked man does not find joy or contentment in God.

questions.question: Job expresses a desire to maintain his integrity until what point?
questions.explanation: Job 27:5 states, 'till I die I will not remove mine integrity from me,' indicating his commitment to righteousness until his last breath.

questions.question: True or False: Job believes that God will hear the cry of the hypocrite when trouble comes upon him, according to Job 27:9.
questions.explanation: Job 27:9 questions whether God will hear the cry of the hypocrite, implying he does not believe God will respond positively.

questions.question: True or False: Job states that the rich man will face mockery and scorn from others according to Job 27:23.
questions.explanation: Job 27:23 indicates that men will clap their hands at him, showing mockery and disdain for the rich man's downfall.

theological.title: Job Chapter 27 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Job Chapter 27 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 27:3 teach about the relationship between human life and divine presence?
options: Human life is sustained by the spirit of God in a vital and immediate way
Human life is independent of divine influence
Divine presence is only symbolic in human vitality
Human breath is a metaphor for natural vitality without divine involvement
questions.correctAnswer: Human life is sustained by the spirit of God in a vital and immediate way
questions.explanation: Job 27:3 states, 'All the while my breath is in me, and the spirit of God is in my nostrils,' indicating that human life is directly sustained by God's spirit.

questions.question: What doctrine about human integrity and righteousness is taught in Job 27:6?
options: The believer holds fast to righteousness as a testimony to their conscience
Righteousness is often abandoned to avoid suffering
Integrity is relative and changes with circumstances
Human righteousness is insufficient and must be discarded
questions.correctAnswer: The believer holds fast to righteousness as a testimony to their conscience
questions.explanation: Job 27:6 says, 'My righteousness I hold fast, and will not let it go: my heart shall not reproach me so long as I live,' showing the doctrine that integrity is steadfast as evidence of a clear conscience.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning divine justice and the fate of the wicked is taught in Job 27:13?
options: The wicked receive a just heritage of judgment from God
The wicked are ultimately rewarded for their deeds
The fate of the wicked is left to human judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked receive a just heritage of judgment from God
questions.explanation: Job 27:13 states, 'This is the portion of a wicked man with God, and the heritage of oppressors, which they shall receive of the Almighty,' affirming God's just judgment on the wicked.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Job 27:2 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Job 27:2 mentions God as 'who hath taken away my judgment; and the Almighty, who hath vexed my soul,' demonstrating God's sovereign control over human affairs.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Job 27:22 where God is described as not sparing the wicked?
questions.explanation: Job 27:22 states, 'For God shall cast upon him, and not spare,' indicating God's attribute of justice in punishing the wicked.

questions.question: How does Job 27:9 connect to the broader biblical theme of divine responsiveness to human suffering?
options: It questions the expectation that God hears the wicked's cries during trouble
It affirms that God always answers the wicked's prayers
It denies that God listens to any human prayers
It suggests the wicked have a special covenantal relationship with God
questions.correctAnswer: It questions the expectation that God hears the wicked's cries during trouble
questions.explanation: Job 27:9 asks, 'Will God hear his cry when trouble cometh upon him?' which connects to biblical themes regarding divine justice and selective responsiveness based on righteousness.

questions.question: In what way does Job 27:18 prepare for New Testament teaching on the fleeting nature of earthly riches?
options: By illustrating that wealth is fragile and temporary as a moth-eaten house
By teaching that earthly riches are eternal and guaranteed
By denying any connection between wealth and divine judgment
By asserting that riches are a sign of divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: By illustrating that wealth is fragile and temporary as a moth-eaten house
questions.explanation: Job 27:18 uses the metaphor of a house eaten by moths to show the impermanence of wealth, a theme echoed in the New Testament's warnings about treasures on earth (e.g., Matthew 6:19-20).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Job 27:4 and Job 27:5 teach about human integrity in the face of adversity?
options: Integrity is preserved through refusal to speak wickedness and by not justifying the wicked
Integrity is flexible and can be compromised for peace
Integrity is irrelevant to divine judgment
One should justify others to maintain social harmony
questions.correctAnswer: Integrity is preserved through refusal to speak wickedness and by not justifying the wicked
questions.explanation: Job 27:4 states 'My lips shall not speak wickedness,' and 27:5 says 'God forbid that I should justify you,' together teaching steadfast personal integrity despite external pressures.

questions.question: What doctrine about the destiny of the wicked is taught by combining Job 27:14 and Job 27:15?
options: The wicked’s offspring will suffer and their family line will experience death without mourning
The wicked’s descendants will prosper and be happy
God will bless the wicked’s family abundantly
The wicked’s progeny will be shielded from judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked’s offspring will suffer and their family line will experience death without mourning
questions.explanation: Job 27:14 says children 'shall not be satisfied with bread,' and 27:15 says 'his widows shall not weep,' indicating judgment extends to the wicked’s descendants with suffering and loss.

questions.question: What combined teaching about divine judgment and human wealth is found in Job 27:16 and Job 27:17?
options: The wicked may amass wealth, but the just will ultimately possess and divide it
Wealth guarantees divine favor and eternal possession
The accumulation of wealth is an indication of righteousness
The innocent will be deprived of wealth by the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked may amass wealth, but the just will ultimately possess and divide it
questions.explanation: Job 27:16 notes the wicked heap silver, but 27:17 says 'the just shall put it on,' teaching that divine justice reallocates wealth from the wicked to the righteous.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Job 27:8-10 implies that hypocrites can expect salvation despite their false piety. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Hypocrites have no true hope because God will take away their soul and will not delight in them
Hypocrites are always granted salvation if they call on God
God ignores whether one is hypocritical or sincere in their prayers
Hypocrites are assured of God's mercy despite their deeds
questions.correctAnswer: Hypocrites have no true hope because God will take away their soul and will not delight in them
questions.explanation: Job 27:8-10 questions the hope of the hypocrite, affirming that God will not hear or delight in their calls, denying them salvation based on false piety.

questions.question: What doctrine does Job 27:12 teach about human vanity and divine revelation?
options: Despite seeing God's truth, people remain vain and reject it
Human beings naturally embrace divine truth when revealed
Vanity is unrelated to knowledge of God
Divine revelation always results in human repentance
questions.correctAnswer: Despite seeing God's truth, people remain vain and reject it
questions.explanation: Job 27:12 states, 'Behold, all ye yourselves have seen it; why then are ye thus altogether vain?' showing that knowledge of God does not guarantee humility or repentance.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Job 27:23 where men mock the wicked at their downfall?
questions.explanation: Job 27:23 describes how men 'shall clap their hands at him, and shall hiss him out of his place,' emphasizing God's justice in allowing the wicked's disgrace.

questions.question: What theological implication does Job 27:19 have regarding the ultimate fate of the rich who are wicked?
options: Though rich, the wicked will not be gathered or preserved in death
Riches guarantee a peaceful and secure death
The rich are exempt from divine judgment
Death is a reward for the wicked rich
questions.correctAnswer: Though rich, the wicked will not be gathered or preserved in death
questions.explanation: Job 27:19 states, 'The rich man shall lie down, but he shall not be gathered,' signifying that wealth does not secure a peaceful or sanctified death for the wicked.

questions.question: How do Job 27:20 and Job 27:21 together portray God's control over the fate of the wicked?
options: God is sovereign, using natural forces like tempest and east wind to remove the wicked from their place
The wicked control their own destiny independent of God
God passively observes the wicked’s downfall
The forces of nature act randomly without divine purpose
questions.correctAnswer: God is sovereign, using natural forces like tempest and east wind to remove the wicked from their place
questions.explanation: Verses 20 and 21 describe terrors, tempest, and east wind carrying the wicked away, illustrating God's sovereign hand in their destruction.
